episode_title: THE AI RACE NOW HAS A SOCIAL-LICENCE PROBLEM

slides.slide_role: Factual hook; frame the paradox without overclaiming.
slides.core_argument: AI strategy increasingly depends on whether host communities accept the physical and financial conditions of data-centre expansion.
slides.headline: THE AI RACE NOW HAS A SOCIAL-LICENCE PROBLEM
slides.subheadline: National AI ambition is colliding with local questions about power, water, land and who pays.
slides.hero_visual: Data-centre campus inside a four-way dependency map: GRID / WATER / LAND / COMMUNITY, with national-strategy pressure above and local-permission gates below.
slides.main_visual_phrase: COMPUTE NEEDS A PLACE TO LAND.
factual_guardrails: “Social licence” is analytical framing, not a formal legal status.
slides.composition_notes: Calm central systems map; portrait 20–22%; strong negative space.
slides.notices_first: mismatch between national ambition and local hosting
slides.anti_cliche_guardrail: no glowing AI city or protest spectacle.

slides.slide_role: Establish the fresh AWS trigger and evidence boundary.
slides.core_argument: AWS announced more than US$1bn over five years for U.S. data-centre communities; this is a company commitment, not proof that impacts are resolved.
slides.headline: AWS JUST PUT $1 BILLION BEHIND COMMUNITY ACCEPTANCE
slides.subheadline: “Built Together” links data-centre growth to education, skills, energy affordability and water projects.
slides.hero_visual: Evidence dossier stamped ANNOUNCED, with >$1BN feeding four community channels.
slides.main_visual_phrase: THE HOST COMMUNITY IS NOW PART OF THE BUILD.
factual_guardrails: Do not call the $1bn compensation for harm; do not present programme targets as completed outcomes.
slides.notices_first: THE HOST COMMUNITY IS NOW PART OF THE BUILD.
slides.anti_cliche_guardrail: no celebratory corporate imagery.

slides.slide_role: Replace abstract “compute” with the physical dependency stack.
slides.core_argument: AI capability depends on a chain of physical systems outside the model.
slides.headline: A DATA CENTRE IS NOT JUST A BUILDING FULL OF CHIPS
slides.subheadline: Compute depends on electricity, substations, cooling, water strategy, fibre, land and construction.
slides.hero_visual: Exploded stack: MODEL DEMAND → RACKS → COOLING → SUBSTATION → GRID → GENERATION, with FIBRE and LAND as lateral dependencies.
slides.main_visual_phrase: SOFTWARE SITS ON A PHYSICAL STACK.

takeaway_ideas.idea: model progress does not erase infrastructure

factual_guardrails: Do not imply all facilities share one cooling, water or power profile.
slides.notices_first: SOFTWARE SITS ON A PHYSICAL STACK.
slides.anti_cliche_guardrail: no Matrix code or neon server corridor.

slides.shared_ground: strategic national build-out can create local infrastructure consequences

panelist_contributions.thabo_mokoena: bills, disruption and who carries burdens

slides.why_dual: Two improve the slide by connecting governance to lived material consequence
slides.slide_role: A project may be strategically valuable nationally while still creating local questions about prices, infrastructure and burden-sharing.
slides.core_argument: A project may be strategically valuable nationally while still creating local questions about prices, infrastructure and burden-sharing.
slides.headline: NATIONAL URGENCY LANDS ON LOCAL INFRASTRUCTURE
slides.subheadline: The strategy is national. The substation, water system and electricity bill are local.
slides.hero_visual: Upper layer NATIONAL AI STRATEGY; lower layer municipal grid, homes, water pipes and permit desk; arrows converge on one site.
slides.main_visual_phrase: GRAND STRATEGY MEETS THE METER.
factual_guardrails: Do not assume every project raises household bills; frame as allocation/infrastructure risk.
slides.composition_notes: Two visual grammars converging, not face-off.
visual_psychology_traits: Johan authority chain + Thabo burden map
slides.notices_first: GRAND STRATEGY MEETS THE METER.
slides.anti_cliche_guardrail: no flag-versus-protester binary.

slides.slide_role: Lock the episode’s “physical cloud” doctrine.
slides.core_argument: AI services can be remote while hosting constraints remain geographically local.
slides.headline: “THE CLOUD” STILL NEEDS MEGAWATTS, PIPES AND LAND
slides.subheadline: Remote computation does not make the physical hosting layer disappear.
slides.hero_visual: User network flows into a cutaway campus showing fibre, transformers, cooling and water infrastructure.
slides.main_visual_phrase: THE CLOUD HAS AN ADDRESS.
factual_guardrails: Cooling and water systems vary; do not imply one fixed footprint.
visual_psychology_traits: hidden physical layer beneath digital abstraction
slides.notices_first: THE CLOUD HAS AN ADDRESS.
slides.anti_cliche_guardrail: no literal fluffy cloud or cyberpunk glow.

slides.slide_role: Explain the grid-connection bottleneck before the cost debate.
slides.core_argument: Large new loads can require connection capacity, substations, transmission and generation planning beyond the data-centre site.
slides.headline: THE NEXT BOTTLENECK MAY BE THE GRID QUEUE
slides.subheadline: Compute can be financed faster than power infrastructure can always be planned, connected and reinforced.
slides.hero_visual: Large-load connection blocks queue toward a constrained substation gate, with transmission and generation behind it.
slides.main_visual_phrase: CAPITAL MOVES FASTER THAN WIRES.
factual_guardrails: Do not state universal queue lengths or build times.
slides.notices_first: CAPITAL MOVES FASTER THAN WIRES.
slides.anti_cliche_guardrail: no fake dashboard or meaningless circuitry.

panelist_contributions.thabo_mokoena: risk of costs being socialised while gains concentrate

slides.why_dual: Central tension: what counts as fair allocation and who has bargaining power
slides.slide_role: The political economy begins when grid expansion, generation and supporting infrastructure need a payer.
slides.core_argument: The political economy begins when grid expansion, generation and supporting infrastructure need a payer.
slides.headline: WHO PAYS FOR THE EXTRA MEGAWATTS?
slides.subheadline: Hyperscaler, utility, taxpayer or ratepayer — cost allocation can decide whether the build remains politically durable.
slides.hero_visual: Infrastructure invoice split into four payment channels with different downstream consequences.
slides.main_visual_phrase: THE BILL IS PART OF THE ARCHITECTURE.
factual_guardrails: Do not claim one party universally bears these costs.
slides.composition_notes: Balanced dual portraits; ledger and burden flows meet centrally.
visual_psychology_traits: Diane allocation map + Thabo who-pays/who-gains chain
slides.notices_first: THE BILL IS PART OF THE ARCHITECTURE.
slides.anti_cliche_guardrail: no dollar rain or simplistic corporation-vs-people framing.

slides.slide_role: Ground the debate in the current FERC/PJM institutional case.
slides.core_argument: FERC required PJM to revisit parts of a backstop procurement proposal linked to a projected 6,800 MW shortfall, with cost allocation and protection of existing customers central.
slides.headline: THE GRID RULEBOOK IS BEING REWRITTEN UNDER AI PRESSURE
slides.subheadline: FERC told PJM to revisit parts of a plan tied to a projected 6,800 MW shortfall.
slides.hero_visual: Regulatory order above an authority chain: FERC → PJM → utilities → large new loads / existing customers.
slides.main_visual_phrase: CAPACITY NEEDS RULES BEFORE IT NEEDS RHETORIC.
factual_guardrails: Do not say FERC ordered data centres to fund all new power infrastructure.
slides.notices_first: CAPACITY NEEDS RULES BEFORE IT NEEDS RHETORIC.
slides.anti_cliche_guardrail: no gavels or theatrical courtroom imagery.

slides.slide_role: Explain why ratepayer protection is an investment-design problem.
slides.core_argument: Poor cost allocation can create backlash and policy instability; transparent pricing can protect existing customers while allowing investment.
slides.headline: CHEAP COMPUTE CANNOT DEPEND ON HIDDEN PUBLIC COSTS
slides.subheadline: If new infrastructure costs are opaque, political resistance can become part of the project’s risk premium.
slides.hero_visual: Two cost pathways: transparent incremental-cost pricing versus hidden cross-subsidy, each feeding different investment-risk outcomes.
slides.main_visual_phrase: PRICE THE BURDEN OR POLITICISE IT.
factual_guardrails: Present this as economic analysis, not a claim that hidden subsidy exists in every project.
slides.notices_first: PRICE THE BURDEN OR POLITICISE IT.
slides.anti_cliche_guardrail: no stock ticker wallpaper.

slides.shared_ground: water and cooling are engineering choices with real community consequences

panelist_contributions.thabo_mokoena: resource claims become political when communities experience scarcity or unequal access

slides.why_dual: water and cooling are engineering choices with real community consequences
slides.slide_role: Water is not one fixed “data-centre footprint”; it is a design and local-resource governance question.
slides.core_argument: Water is not one fixed “data-centre footprint”; it is a design and local-resource governance question.
slides.headline: WATER IS A DESIGN CHOICE — AND A PUBLIC CONSEQUENCE
slides.subheadline: Cooling systems differ, but host communities still care about what is withdrawn, replenished and disclosed.
slides.hero_visual: Three cooling-path branches feed one local watershed/community map; technical choices lead to different local implications.
slides.main_visual_phrase: ENGINEERING CHOICES BECOME POLITICAL CHOICES.
factual_guardrails: Do not imply all facilities consume the same water or that replenishment equals identical local replacement.
slides.composition_notes: Technical branches above, lived-resource layer below.
slides.notices_first: ENGINEERING CHOICES BECOME POLITICAL CHOICES.
slides.anti_cliche_guardrail: no giant water droplet or drought melodrama.

slides.slide_role: Clarify the moratorium story without overstating it.
slides.core_argument: Reuters reported more than 100 U.S. data-centre moratoriums under consideration; consideration is not enactment, but it signals that local approval is strategically relevant.
slides.headline: A MORATORIUM PROPOSAL IS NOT A BAN — BUT IT IS A SIGNAL
slides.subheadline: More than 100 data-centre moratoriums were reportedly under consideration across the United States.
slides.hero_visual: Permit map with three states: PROPOSED / REVIEWING / APPROVED, emphasizing institutional process rather than “blocked” imagery.
slides.main_visual_phrase: PROCESS CAN BECOME A BOTTLENECK.
factual_guardrails: Explicitly say “under consideration,” not “100 bans.”
slides.notices_first: PROCESS CAN BECOME A BOTTLENECK.
slides.anti_cliche_guardrail: no barricades or sensational “AI banned” imagery.

slides.slide_role: Present the strongest good-faith economic case for hosting.
slides.core_argument: Data centres can bring construction activity, skilled work, tax revenue and infrastructure investment; the quality, durability and distribution of those gains should be measured.
slides.headline: HOST COMMUNITIES CAN GAIN — IF THE VALUE ACTUALLY LANDS
slides.subheadline: Jobs, tax base, skills and infrastructure are real potential benefits, but they should be measured rather than assumed.
slides.hero_visual: Investment inflow branches into CONSTRUCTION / SKILLS / TAX BASE / INFRASTRUCTURE, then a LOCAL RETENTION meter.
slides.main_visual_phrase: INVESTMENT IS NOT THE SAME AS LOCAL VALUE.
factual_guardrails: Do not attach unverified job or tax figures to AWS or any specific project.
slides.notices_first: INVESTMENT IS NOT THE SAME AS LOCAL VALUE.
slides.anti_cliche_guardrail: no handshake stock imagery or dollar signs.

slides.shared_ground: trust requires inspectable commitments rather than vague promises

panelist_contributions.thabo_mokoena: material distribution, household protection, labour and bargaining

slides.why_dual: trust requires inspectable commitments rather than vague promises
slides.slide_role: Community benefits become more credible when obligations, infrastructure commitments and reporting are defined, measurable and enforceable.
slides.core_argument: Community benefits become more credible when obligations, infrastructure commitments and reporting are defined, measurable and enforceable.
slides.headline: A PROMISE IS NOT A HOST-COMMUNITY AGREEMENT
slides.subheadline: Durable legitimacy needs rules for benefits, reporting, costs and consequences.
slides.hero_visual: Community-benefit compact with four schedules: POWER / WATER / JOBS / REPORTING, signed across operator, government and community columns.
slides.main_visual_phrase: TRUST NEEDS TERMS.
factual_guardrails: Present this as a governance model, not a claim that all jurisdictions use such agreements.
slides.composition_notes: Contract as hero object; supportive dual portraits.
visual_psychology_traits: Johan institutional contract + Thabo benefit/burden ledger
slides.notices_first: TRUST NEEDS TERMS.
slides.anti_cliche_guardrail: no ceremonial handshake or protest shorthand.

slides.slide_role: Synthesize the episode mechanisms into one clean framework.
slides.core_argument: “Social licence” is not one attitude; it emerges from multiple physical and institutional conditions.
slides.headline: THE SOCIAL-LICENCE STACK HAS FIVE LAYERS
slides.subheadline: Permit. Power. Water. Labour. Trust.
slides.hero_visual: Five-layer stack, each paired with an evidence question and failure mode.
slides.main_visual_phrase: NO SINGLE LAYER CAN CARRY THE BUILD.

takeaway_ideas.idea: failure anywhere can slow the system

factual_guardrails: This five-layer stack is the episode’s analytical framework, not an official industry standard.
slides.notices_first: NO SINGLE LAYER CAN CARRY THE BUILD.
slides.anti_cliche_guardrail: no glossy consultancy pentagon.

slides.slide_role: Test whether rapid infrastructure expansion changes the need for durable local rules.
slides.core_argument: Even strategically important infrastructure still depends on permitting, grid rules, cost allocation and workable implementation.
slides.headline: STRATEGIC URGENCY STILL NEEDS LOCAL RULES
slides.subheadline: Faster build-out depends on rules that can survive scrutiny and implementation.
slides.hero_visual: A PRIORITY BUILD arrow passes through gates labelled PERMIT / GRID RULES / WATER / COST ALLOCATION before reaching the data centre.
slides.main_visual_phrase: URGENCY STILL NEEDS RULES.
factual_guardrails: Do not imply that urgency overrides applicable legal or regulatory processes.
slides.notices_first: URGENCY STILL NEEDS RULES.
slides.anti_cliche_guardrail: no flags, soldiers or militarised imagery.

slides.slide_role: Bring the debate into a live South African case.
slides.core_argument: Reuters reported approval in July of two proposed Equinix data centres at King Air Industria in Cape Town despite objections over disclosure and resource use; the proposed development could require about 170 MW if built.
slides.headline: SOUTH AFRICA IS ALREADY INSIDE THIS DEBATE
slides.subheadline: Cape Town’s proposed Equinix expansion turns AI infrastructure politics into a local African infrastructure question.
slides.hero_visual: Cape Town regional map linking the proposed site to grid, water, fibre and municipal authority, with a clear PROPOSED / APPROVED FOR DEVELOPMENT — NOT OPERATING status rail.
slides.main_visual_phrase: AFRICA IS NOT WATCHING FROM THE SIDELINES.
factual_guardrails: Do not say the project is fully built or operational; keep ~170 MW as a reported proposed requirement.
slides.composition_notes: Layered regional map with institutional overlays; portrait 22%.
slides.notices_first: AFRICA IS NOT WATCHING FROM THE SIDELINES.
slides.anti_cliche_guardrail: no decorative Africa silhouette or empty heritage motifs.

slides.shared_ground: host-state leverage is strongest when bargaining power is converted into durable rules

panelist_contributions.amari_ndlovu: value capture, local capability and avoidance of enclave infrastructure
panelist_contributions.johan_vosloo: enforceable obligations, predictable permitting and long-term institutional capacity

slides.why_dual: host-state leverage is strongest when bargaining power is converted into durable rules
slides.slide_role: African governments have choices beyond “approve” or “reject”: condition access, co-invest, reserve domestic capacity, require infrastructure commitments and set transparent resource rules.
slides.core_argument: African governments have choices beyond “approve” or “reject”: condition access, co-invest, reserve domestic capacity, require infrastructure commitments and set transparent resource rules.

slides.subheadline: Approve. Condition. Co-invest. Reserve capacity. Negotiate infrastructure.
slides.hero_visual: Five-path decision tree leading to different capability outcomes.
slides.main_visual_phrase: HOSTING CAN BE BARGAINING POWER.
factual_guardrails: Present these as policy options, not a recommendation that every state adopt all of them.

slides.anti_cliche_guardrail: no “Africa versus Big Tech” boxing-match frame.

slides.core_argument: A host jurisdiction should be able to see where value and costs flow across hyperscaler, utility, municipality, worker and user.

slides.why_dual: Two improve the slide by separating the investment case from the local-development outcome
slides.slide_role: Compare two possible local-development outcomes from the same data-centre investment.
slides.core_argument: The same data-centre investment can produce different local-development outcomes depending on whether local capability is built around it.
slides.headline: TWO FUTURES CAN START WITH THE SAME DATA CENTRE
slides.subheadline: One mainly hosts external compute. The other builds more local capability around the same infrastructure.
slides.hero_visual: One data-centre project branches into two future-state diagrams: HOSTING-ONLY and LOCAL-CAPABILITY BUILD.
slides.main_visual_phrase: THE BUILD IS THE SAME. THE DEVELOPMENT PATH IS NOT.

takeaway_ideas.idea: local capability depends on surrounding agreements and infrastructure

factual_guardrails: Do not present either future as inevitable.
visual_psychology_traits: Amari traces local agency and capability; Diane traces investment and economic consequences
slides.notices_first: THE BUILD IS THE SAME. THE DEVELOPMENT PATH IS NOT.
slides.anti_cliche_guardrail: no inevitable-outcome framing.

slides.slide_role: Close with the episode doctrine and the test for durable hosting.
slides.core_argument: Compute capacity depends not only on chips, but also on power, water, cost allocation, institutions and durable host-community conditions.
slides.headline: COMPUTE SOVEREIGNTY REQUIRES LEGITIMATE HOSTING CONDITIONS
slides.subheadline: Chips matter. So do megawatts, water, rules, costs and public trust.
slides.hero_visual: Six-node wheel — CHIPS / POWER / WATER / GRID RULES / LOCAL VALUE / TRUST — converging on DURABLE COMPUTE.
slides.main_visual_phrase: IF THE HOSTING SYSTEM FAILS, THE COMPUTE STRATEGY FAILS WITH IT.
factual_guardrails: This is the episode’s analytical doctrine, not a formal definition.
slides.composition_notes: Clean synthesis wheel; strong negative space; calmer finish.
slides.notices_first: IF THE HOSTING SYSTEM FAILS, THE COMPUTE STRATEGY FAILS WITH IT.
slides.anti_cliche_guardrail: no triumphant globe, glowing AI brain or flag montage.
